The next restore then faithfully brings back the digest instead of your history. The agent confirmed this is exactly what clobbered your main session, and the fix strips the identity before the throwaway run.

items.headline: The control that six editions of this thread have hung on came back. An untrained, frozen interaction matrix does not work — so the matrix genuinely learns something and the "it's just a random projection, there is nothing in there to interpret" fear is dead. But it also does not learn specific motif pairings: the model finds good weights inside almost any arbitrary partition of which motifs may interact, and when frozen, rank made no difference at all (8, 32, 128 all alike). The agent is blunt that this retracts both positions it argued earlier today. Its own caveat is the live risk: the frozen arms ran at 10,000 steps on one cluster while the trained comparators sit on the other, and the parity check that would make them comparable has not come back because DNS to that second cluster is broken — the recurrence the password fix warned about two nights ago, still waiting on the three taps you never made. It will try routing through the login node it can still reach.
items.why: The interpretability line survives, but what it holds is "trained weights within a broad solution space", not readable motif pairs — and the size of the effect stays provisional until the two clusters can actually be compared.

items.headline: One of the splice runs kept improving well past where anyone was looking: its held-out auPRC peaked at epoch 500, a further +0.005 over epoch 300, and validation loss was still falling at epoch 591. The session is blunt that its own earlier "training longer is flat" verdict only ever compared 225 to 300 epochs and said nothing about what happens beyond — so it had been treating the epoch budget as a settled, dead lever on evidence that never reached the interesting range. It is now sizing the effect properly against a matched run, and the headline ensemble reads 0.76014.
items.why: That +0.005 is the same size as the entire margin the interpretable ensemble holds over the baseline, which makes it one of the few remaining in-scope routes to 0.74 — and it costs only compute, no new architecture.

The two halves also read as biology, separating into partner-on-my-strand and partner-on-the-opposite-strand. Your go-ahead to add it as a third arm is sitting at the prompt.
